Discovery call — Summit Peak Roofing (Denver, CO). Attendees: Marco Delgado (Ridgeline AI), Rick Alvarez (owner, Summit Peak Roofing), Tasha Greene (office manager).

Marco: Thanks for jumping on, Rick. I'm not going to ask about pain points. What's your itch? The thing you know is eating hours every week.

Rick: Insurance claims. Hands down. We're a storm restoration shop, about 85 percent of our jobs are hail or wind claims. After the June hailstorm we had 140 open claims. Every one of them needs the adjuster chased, the supplement written, photos organized, and the homeowner kept in the loop. Tasha and I are doing that at nine at night.

Tasha: My day is basically: open the claims spreadsheet, see who hasn't heard back from the adjuster in five days, email them, call State Farm or Allstate, sit on hold, update the sheet. Then the homeowners call me asking where their check is. I probably spend 25 hours a week on follow-ups alone.

Marco: Walk me through a supplement.

Rick: The adjuster writes an Xactimate estimate and they always miss stuff. Drip edge, ice and water shield, starter strip, code upgrades like the second layer tear-off, O&P. I compare their scope to our measurement report from EagleView, list every missing line item with the code requirement, attach photos, and send it back. Each supplement takes me about 90 minutes. We leave probably $3,000 to $6,000 per job on the table when we don't supplement.

Marco: Where does the data live?

Tasha: Jobs are in AccuLynx. Claim numbers, adjuster names and emails are in a Google Sheet because AccuLynx doesn't track adjuster follow-ups well. Photos are in CompanyCam. Everything comes in through the office Gmail.

Marco: What would you want waiting for you at 7am?

Rick: A list of every claim that's stalled, who the adjuster is, how many days since last contact, and a follow-up email already drafted that I just approve. And a draft supplement for any new adjuster estimate that came in overnight.

Tasha: And a weekly text update to homeowners so they stop calling me. Something like, your claim is with the adjuster, we followed up Tuesday, next step is the supplement review.

Marco: Anything the agent should never do?

Rick: Never send anything to an insurance carrier without me approving it. Never promise a homeowner a dollar amount or a date. And never talk about deductibles — that's a legal landmine in Colorado, we can't waive or absorb them.

Marco: Who else might want this?

Rick: Honestly every roofer in my BNI group has the same problem. Smaller crews would pay for a claims follow-up assistant. Public adjusters too.

Marco: Great. I'll have your claims assistant set up today and you should see your first stalled-claims report tomorrow morning.
